entries.title: `dark/config/declare.py` is the declaration primitive: `setting()` wraps `dataclasses.field` and a setting without description, unit and admissible values is not constructible
entries.body:
Module: `dark/config/declare.py`. Stdlib only — `dataclasses`, `typing`. No third-party dependency: Python 3.12 dataclass field metadata already carries arbitrary declaration data, so a settings framework (pydantic, attrs, dynaconf, hydra) buys nothing this project needs and costs a dependency, a schema DSL and a second way to be wrong.

Two public names.

```python
@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class Setting:
    description: str      # what this controls, one sentence, reader-facing
    unit: str             # "m", "s", "Hz", "rad", "1" for dimensionless — never empty
    admissible: str       # reader-facing admissibility, e.g. "> 0", "in [0, 1]"
    check: Callable[[object], bool]   # the machine-checkable form of `admissible`
    provisional: Provisional | None = None

def setting(
    default: object,
    *,
    description: str,
    unit: str,
    admissible: str,
    check: Callable[[object], bool],
    provisional: Provisional | None = None,
) -> Any:
    """Returns dataclasses.field(default=default, metadata={"dark": Setting(...)})."""
```

The return annotation is `Any` deliberately — the standard idiom that lets a `field()` sentinel stand where the field's own type is annotated, and the only spelling mypy `strict` accepts without a plugin.

**Not-constructible, mechanically.** All five descriptive arguments are keyword-only and have no defaults, so `setting(3.0)` is a `TypeError` at import. `Setting.__post_init__` additionally raises `ValueError` on an empty or whitespace-only `description`, `unit` or `admissible`. A·02 asks that introducing a setting without its description be impossible rather than discouraged; a required keyword argument plus a constructor guard is the whole of that, and it costs four lines.

**`admissible` and `check` are the same fact in two forms and that duplication is deliberate**, because one is for a reader and one is for the resolver, and no mechanism in stdlib derives readable prose from a predicate. The pairing is kept adjacent in one call so they are edited together; nothing projects one from the other.

**Sequence-valued settings are tuples.** A frozen dataclass default must be immutable, and a tuple default needs no `default_factory`, so `default_factory` is not a parameter of `setting()`. If a mutable default ever becomes genuinely necessary, it is added then.

Ordering note: `declare.py` imports nothing else in this package except `Provisional`, which lives in the same module. Everything else in the slice imports it. No same-layer edge records that — an edge into this slice would have to be an emission, and a slice does not emit into itself.

S\u00b701.title: Every artifact must be intelligible to someone arriving with no prior context
Provisionally taken decisions must be revisable without rewriting what was built on them
A configuration explains itself to a reader, including the settings that were left at their defaults
A setting's meaning, unit and admissible values are declared where the setting is declared, and every reader-facing explanation is projected from those declarations
S\u00b701.body:
What a setting controls, the unit it is expressed in, and the values it admits are part of the setting's own declaration. There is exactly one place in the system a setting can be introduced, and introducing one there without its description is not expressible — not discouraged, not checked after the fact, not possible.

Any explanation a reader is shown is derived from those declarations at the moment it is produced, never authored beside them. A separately maintained description is a second copy of a fact, and the copy a human maintains is the one that goes stale; that failure is silent and looks exactly like correct documentation, which is what makes it worth designing out rather than policing.

Three properties then hold without anyone enforcing them: the reader-facing explanation cannot describe a setting that does not exist, cannot omit one that does, and cannot disagree with the running system about a unit.

The boundary this draws is that description is data owned by the declaration site, not prose owned by a document.

dark/config/declare.py.title: `Provisional` is a declaration-site attribute holding claim and revisit condition together, and one without the other raises
dark/config/declare.py.body:
Module: `dark/config/declare.py`, beside `Setting` — provisionality is an attribute of a declaration, so it lives where declarations live, not in a register module of its own.

```python
@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class Provisional:
    claim: str          # what was decided provisionally, in one sentence
    revisit_when: str   # the condition that would trigger reversing it
```

`__post_init__` raises `ValueError` unless both fields are non-empty after `.strip()`. A·03 requires that recording provisionality without its trigger not be expressible; two required positional-or-keyword fields with no defaults plus that guard is exactly that, and there is no constructor path that yields a mark with a blank trigger.

**Frozen and `slots=True`, therefore safely shareable.** A `Provisional` attached to a setting is copied nowhere; the same instance is referenced by the declaration, by the projected `LegendEntry`, and by every merged legend downstream. Immutability is what makes that sharing correct rather than a mutation hazard.

**There is no registry of open decisions in this package, and adding one would be the defect A·03 names.** Provisional marks are discovered by walking the declarations (see the legend projection entry), never by reading a list someone maintains. The consequence worth stating for later sessions: to find every provisional decision in the system you render the legend, and the answer cannot be stale because it is computed.

**Scope, and a judgement call.** A·03 says provisionality attaches to "the setting, the stored record of a run, the reported quantity". This slice owns only the settings case in band; for a stored record or a reported quantity, the mark travels as a `LegendEntry.provisional` inside the legend that the producing stage carries, which is the carry-through mechanism rather than a second one. A stage that wants to mark a decision of its own that is not a setting constructs a `LegendEntry` with a `Provisional` and merges it into the legend it emits — `legend.py` supports this, and no further machinery is specified for it.

tests.title: A setting declared without its description, unit, admissible text or check is not constructible
tests.purpose: the guarantee is supposed to be mechanical, not a convention — a declaration that omits its description must fail at import, not lint clean and ship undescribed
tests.body: Declare a setting supplying only a default value and nothing else. The declaration raises `TypeError`, and it raises when the module is imported rather than when the setting is first read. The same holds when any one of description, unit, admissible text or check is omitted while the others are supplied, and when any of them is passed positionally rather than by keyword.

tests.title: A setting whose description, unit or admissible text is blank or whitespace is rejected at construction
tests.purpose: required-keyword-argument is satisfied by `description=""`, which is how an undescribed setting gets past the first guard; the unit is the field that gets the empty string, since dimensionless tempts one
tests.body: Declare a setting supplying every descriptive argument but with an empty string for the description. Construction raises `ValueError`. The same holds for a string of only whitespace, and independently for the unit and for the admissible text. A dimensionless setting states a unit rather than leaving it empty.

tests.title: A declared setting's default and its full declaration record are both recoverable from the dataclass field
tests.purpose: this is the whole coupling the legend projection rests on — if the record is stored anywhere but on the field, every projection has to be told about settings separately, which is the second copy the slice exists to prevent
tests.body: Declare a dataclass with one field declared as a setting. The field's default is the value that was declared as the default, so constructing the dataclass with no arguments yields that value. Reading the field's declaration metadata yields the declaration record, and its description, unit, admissible text, check and provisional mark are the ones that were supplied. The check is callable and answers for a value as it was defined to.

audit.rule: any file touched outside editable_paths is a write this unit never declared, and is almost always a dependency nobody declared. Files inside it may be shared with the units named in `overlap`, which is why those must not be worked at the same time -- but each of them declares the file too, so a write here is still within this unit's own write set
